Bacterial Canker shows scorching/browning leaf margins. Not matching. Let me check Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus (second reference) and Verticillium Wilt.

This CMV reference (Bugwood_18) is an extremely strong match to the test image. Both show field-level views of stunted, bushy, low-growing tomato plants in rows. The field appearance is nearly identical. The Bugwood IDs are even from the same series (1568048 vs 1568052).

Let me use my final view to confirm by checking Verticillium Wilt.

Verticillium Wilt shows V-shaped leaf lesions, completely different from the test image.

## Summary

I viewed 8 reference images across 7 classes. The evidence is clear:

- **Test image**: Field-level view of uniformly stunted, bushy, low-growing tomato plants across rows. Plants are green but very short and compact.
- **Best match**: Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus reference (Bugwood_18, ID 1568048) is nearly identical to the test image (ID 1568052) — same field-level view of stunted, bushy rows. These are from the same Bugwood image series.
- **KB confirmation**: CMV causes "stunting, mosaic patterns... plants appear lighter in color, bushy and stunted" — perfectly describes what we see.
- **All wilt diseases** (Bacterial Wilt, Southern Bacterial Wilt, Bacterial Canker, Verticillium Wilt, Southern Blight) showed dramatic drooping/collapse, browning, or death — none matched the uniform stunting pattern.
